items.question: What health insurance plans do we offer?
items.answer:
We offer three main types of health insurance plans:

1. Individual Health Plans - Coverage for you and your dependents with flexible deductible options ($500-$5,000)
2. Family Health Plans - Comprehensive coverage for entire families with shared deductibles, save up to 30% vs individual policies
3. Group Health Plans - Employer-sponsored coverage with competitive rates and comprehensive benefits

All plans include preventive care, emergency services, hospitalization, prescription drugs, and mental health services.

items.question: What is the difference between our HMO and PPO health plans?
items.answer:
We offer both HMO and PPO plans with distinct features:

HMO (Health Maintenance Organization):
- Lower monthly premiums (starting at $250/month)
- Requires primary care physician (PCP) selection
- Referrals needed for specialists
- Network-only coverage (except emergencies)
- No claim forms needed
- Best for: Budget-conscious individuals who don't mind coordinated care

PPO (Preferred Provider Organization):
- Higher premiums (starting at $400/month) but more flexibility
- No PCP requirement or referrals needed
- See any doctor, in or out of network
- Out-of-network coverage at 60-70% (vs 80-90% in-network)
- May need to file claims for out-of-network care
- Best for: Those who want maximum flexibility and choice

items.question: What is our health insurance deductible and how does it work?
items.answer:
A health insurance deductible is the amount you pay out-of-pocket before your insurance starts paying. We offer plans with deductibles ranging from $500 to $5,000:

- $500 deductible: Higher monthly premium ($450/mo), lower out-of-pocket
- $1,500 deductible: Mid-tier premium ($350/mo), balanced approach
- $3,000 deductible: Lower premium ($280/mo), higher initial costs
- $5,000 deductible: Lowest premium ($220/mo), best for healthy individuals

How it works:
1. You pay medical bills until you reach your deductible
2. After deductible is met, you pay co-insurance (typically 20%)
3. Insurance pays the rest (typically 80%)
4. Once you hit out-of-pocket maximum, insurance pays 100%

Note: Preventive care is covered at 100% regardless of deductible status.

items.question: What does our health insurance out-of-pocket maximum mean?
items.answer:
The out-of-pocket maximum is the most you'll pay for covered services in a year. After reaching this limit, we pay 100% of covered expenses.

Our out-of-pocket maximums by plan:
- Bronze Plan: $8,700 individual / $17,400 family
- Silver Plan: $7,000 individual / $14,000 family
- Gold Plan: $6,000 individual / $12,000 family
- Platinum Plan: $4,000 individual / $8,000 family

What counts toward out-of-pocket max:
✓ Deductibles
✓ Co-payments
✓ Co-insurance

What does NOT count:
✗ Monthly premiums
✗ Out-of-network care (in most plans)
✗ Services not covered by your plan

Once you reach this limit, you have financial protection for the rest of the year.

items.question: What preventive care services are covered at 100%?
items.answer:
Under the Affordable Care Act, we cover these preventive services at 100% with no deductible or co-pay:

Adult Preventive Care:
- Annual physical exam
- Blood pressure screening
- Cholesterol screening
- Diabetes screening
- Cancer screenings (mammogram, colonoscopy, etc.)
- Depression screening
- Obesity screening and counseling
- Tobacco cessation counseling
- Immunizations (flu, pneumonia, etc.)

Women's Preventive Care:
- Well-woman visits
- Mammograms
- Pap smears
- Contraception
- Prenatal care
- Breastfeeding support

Children's Preventive Care:
- Well-child visits
- Immunizations
- Vision and hearing screening
- Developmental assessments

These services must be from in-network providers to be covered at 100%.

items.question: Do you cover prescription drugs and how do copays work?
items.answer:
Yes, all our health plans include prescription drug coverage with a 4-tier copay structure:

Tier 1 - Generic Drugs:
- 30-day supply: $10 copay
- 90-day supply: $25 copay
- Covers: Generic antibiotics, blood pressure meds, etc.

Tier 2 - Preferred Brand Drugs:
- 30-day supply: $35 copay
- 90-day supply: $90 copay
- Covers: Preferred brand-name drugs

Tier 3 - Non-Preferred Brand Drugs:
- 30-day supply: $70 copay
- 90-day supply: $180 copay
- Covers: Non-preferred brand-name drugs

Tier 4 - Specialty Drugs:
- 30-day supply: 25% co-insurance (max $250)
- Covers: Specialty medications for complex conditions

Mail-order pharmacy available for 90-day supplies at discounted rates. Copays may apply to deductible depending on your plan.

items.question: What mental health services are covered?
items.answer:
We provide comprehensive mental health coverage as part of all health insurance plans:

Outpatient Mental Health:
- Individual therapy: $30 copay per session
- Group therapy: $15 copay per session
- Psychiatric services: $50 copay per visit
- Unlimited visits (no session limits)

Inpatient Mental Health:
- Covered at same rate as medical hospitalization
- $500 copay per admission
- Medically necessary stays fully covered

Substance Abuse Treatment:
- Outpatient programs: $30 copay per visit
- Intensive outpatient (IOP): Covered at 80% after deductible
- Inpatient detox and rehab: $500 copay per admission

Teletherapy:
- Virtual counseling sessions: $25 copay
- 24/7 crisis hotline: No cost

All services must be provided by in-network providers. Pre-authorization may be required for inpatient services.

items.question: Is maternity and childbirth covered?
items.answer:
Yes, maternity care is fully covered under all our health plans as an essential health benefit:

Prenatal Care (100% covered, no deductible):
- All prenatal visits and screenings
- Ultrasounds and lab tests
- Genetic counseling if needed

Labor and Delivery:
- Hospital stay: Standard deductible and co-insurance apply
- Typical cost: $500-$3,000 depending on plan and delivery type
- C-section covered same as vaginal delivery
- Private room upgrade: Additional $200/day

Postpartum Care:
- Follow-up visits covered at 100%
- Breastfeeding support and lactation consulting
- Breast pump coverage (one per pregnancy)

Newborn Care:
- Automatically covered for first 30 days
- Must add baby to policy within 60 days of birth
- No waiting period or medical underwriting

Complications covered same as other medical conditions. NICU stays covered with same cost-sharing as adult hospitalization.
